chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, who said:

I had a nosebleed for a year in Medina, so our companions asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about something that stops the nosebleed. He said to them: 'Give him to drink suwiq of apples.' So they gave me to drink it, and the nosebleed ceased from me.

key_terms.سَوِيق: Suwiq, a thick drink or porridge made from ground grain (often barley) mixed with water or milk

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended remedy for nosebleeds according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the practical medical wisdom of the Imams, illustrating their holistic approach to healing through natural remedies. The specific prescription of apple *suwiq* demonstrates the Shia tradition of valuing both spiritual authority and empirical observation in health matters, reinforcing the concept that the Imams possess comprehensive knowledge of the physical world.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr who said,

‘I had nose-bleed for a year at Al-Medina. So our companions asked Abu Abdullahasws about something which could stop the nose-bleed, so heasws said to them: ‘Make him drink Suweyq of the apples’. So they made me drink it, and the nose-bleed cut-off from me’.
en.sarwar: 6. Abu Ali al-Ash‘ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from ibn Faddal from ibn Bukayr who has said the following: “I

one year suffered nasal hemorrhage in al-Madinah and our people asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al- Salam, about something that can stop nose bleeding. He (the Imam) said, ‘Make him drink sawiq of apples (soup of apples).’ They followed the instruction and my nose bleeding stopped.’”
